$comment: How TransLink's routes are drawn where the GTFS alone doesn't say (packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#routes). Every route in the feed is drawn by default, modelled from its GTFS route_type (buses: GTFS-RT with schedule fallback, coloured by frequency; rail and ferries: along their shapes, in their own colour), keyed by its short name without leading zeros ('025' → '25') or else its long name, labelled '<key> <long name>', in its GTFS route_color (#666666 without one). An entry here overrides any of that for the route it matches, by name (route_long_name / route_short_name, never route_id, which changes between feeds): 'kind' is how vehicles are modelled ('skytrain' = track-level, packages/transit-core/DESIGN.md#track-graph; 'shape' = interpolated along GTFS shapes; 'bus' = GTFS-RT with schedule fallback), 'kinematics' overrides the vehicle settings of the route's mode (config/defaults/kinematics.json, then its operator's), 'color' is the colour it's drawn in, and 'brand' draws a bus route in that colour, as its operator brands it, rather than by frequency (the 99 B-Line and RapidBus R1–R6; rail and ferries always are), unless the viewer colours every route by frequency. The layers panel's Frequent Bus and Fast Bus switches aren't set here: they come from the timetable (apps/web/README.md#header-and-layers). The 99 is orange and every RapidBus the same green, as on TransLink's maps (the GTFS has other shades). 'exclude' leaves routes out of the plan altogether: not drawn, on cards or tracked.
